patients.label: 54-year-old man with type II diabetes mellitus and carbamazepine-induced AGEP complicated by diabetic ketoacidosis

identity_evidence.quote: A 54-year-old patient with multiple comorbidities developed AGEP shortly after initiating carbamazepine therapy for poststroke seizure.

attribution_limitations: The text places carbamazepine initiation 15 days before hospital presentation. The Figure 3 timeline prints a day-numbered axis whose carbamazepine-to-emergency-presentation interval differs from this; image values are recorded only in visual.json. The text itself is also arithmetically tight: the rash began about 13 days after starting the drug, the first febrile episode began with the rash and lasted about 4 days, and fever recurred 2 days before admission, which does not fit a 15-day interval.

The text says complete rash resolution was noted by the fifth day without naming the reference point, and Figure 2 and Figure 3 print their own day labels for resolution; image values are recorded only in visual.json.

Dexamethasone is described as stopped because of rapid glucose fluctuation (b00050), while the discussion describes rapid tapering of systemic steroids once systemic and cutaneous symptoms stabilized (b00074). The two statements are compatible (a rapid taper ends in stopping) and are not a source conflict, but the source does not say whether the stop was abrupt or the end of a taper, nor which reason governed it.
The text prints bicarbonate as 14.13 mmol/l while Table 1 prints the same value as 14.13 mEq/l.
Table 2 scores fever (≥38°C) as +1, while the only temperature stated is an axillary 100.2°F at initial evaluation; the case text also describes intermittent fever.

DRESS is described as "arguing against" and "consistent with not a case of DRESS" after a low retrospective RegiSCAR score, but the authors never use ruled-out or excluded wording for DRESS, and an overlap syndrome is described as having been considered at presentation.
The authors propose that dapagliflozin may have had at most a permissive role in ketosis and that an inflammatory cascade precipitated DKA; these are author hypotheses.
